minutes.headline: Commission heard hours of comment on opening land to firearm hunting, continued the hearing to March 17 on a 4-3 vote, and approved a land gift.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission held a long public forum on revised land use regulations, mostly about expanding firearm hunting to two more properties and about snowmobile access. A motion to continue the hearing to March 17 and post all submitted letters on the website passed 4-3. The commission then continued or approved several wetlands filings, accepted a gift of land from Bright Farms, and ended with a tense exchange between members before going into executive session.

what_happened.line: The commission voted 4-3 to continue the land use hearing to March 17 and to post all letters received on its website.
The hearing drew a long public forum on opening more conservation land to firearm hunting, plus snowmobile access and firearm carry; no vote was taken on the regulations.
The commission voted to accept a gift of parcel B from PSG Realty LLC (Bright Farms), subject to select board approval.
It approved a driveway at 36 Cushing Lane and septic repair plans at Thompson Harbor, and continued the Wu, Proctor Masonry and Northfield Associates filings.
The chair proposed a workshop on the regulations at the next meeting, with members to submit specific language; the meeting ended in executive session on litigation.

why_it_matters: The rules for who may carry firearms and hunt on town conservation land, and on which parcels, have not been decided, so residents who use those trails still have a hearing to attend or write to.
Posting the letters means the written comments become public record, so residents can read what others sent before the hearing resumes.
The land gift still needs select board approval, so the town does not yet hold the parcel.
watch_next: Continued land use regulations hearing on March 17, with a workshop on the regulations planned beforehand.
Select board approval of the Bright Farms land gift, which the commission's acceptance depends on.
